text:
Lina Park: Quick brain dump 1: debating compact preflight strip vs full modal for saving alert routing + suppression rules. Mock: https://img.redwood.dev/ux/preflight_strip.png

Owen Blake: Strip is nice for speed, but visual scan suffers with >4 channels. Maybe cap at 3 and show 'Expand (4 more)'.

Nora Kim: a11y flag: if we keep strip it must still expose all details to screen readers. Add an offscreen list and a meaningful aria-label like 'Notification channels (4)'.

Lina Park: good call. Also copy: header currently 'Review routing' 1 feels vague. Propose 'Review who gets alerted' for clarity.

Owen Blake: CTA wording: first-time flow -> 'Enable notifications', edit flow -> 'Save routing'. Helps users understand side effects.

Nora Kim: live update: when suppression toggles the preview, announce 'Suppression enabled until 06:00 PT' via aria-live=polite. Don't move focus.

Lina Park: UI trade: show small recipient avatars inline to improve scanability. If many, show '+5' overflow.

Owen Blake: technical note: DOM order should match visual order so tabbing is predictable. If we collapse channels, ensure the expand button is reachable before the list.

DesignBot: analytics suggestion: events: preflight_open, preflight_expand_channels, preflight_confirm with props {channel_count, suppression_active, ui_mode}.

Nora Kim: final microcopy idea: tooltip on suppression: 'Suppression pauses notifications during this window. On-call schedules still update recipients.'

Lina Park: action items: Owen prototypes compact strip with expand behavior, Nora writes aria copy and live strings, i'll update copy variants and share updated mock. Back here after PR. :thumbsup:
